counter_direction_note: Reported in both directions. (a) CUBRID parallelizes this scan BETTER than PostgreSQL: 5.31x on 6 units (88% efficiency) against 4.06x on 5+leader (68%), so the serial per-row cost ratio is 3.1297x - WORSE than the 2.4583x parallel-regime F_cpu - and CUBRID's better scaling claws back 1.27x. (b) PostgreSQL spends 14.75% = 1.338 core-s of its executor CPU on per-statement parallel-worker page-table setup and teardown plus 0.298 core-s of per-tuple memory-context churn, 1.636 core-s that CUBRID's threaded model does not pay at all; net of both, F_cpu would be 2.744x rather than 2.458x. (c) Both engines pay about 2.5 core-s to parallelize, for opposite reasons: CUBRID +2.500 core-s (66% its extra page-cache reads), PostgreSQL +2.585 core-s (63% worker fork/teardown). (d) The headline is a statement about a CONFIGURED comparison: at parallelism=12 CUBRID reaches 2.021 s, 1.917x faster than its contracted 3.875 s, and at max_parallel_workers_per_gather=11 PostgreSQL reaches 1.297 s. imp_010_summary: NEW, P1, buffer/IO + parallelism, difficulty LOW, evidence direct A/B. Root cause: scan-resistance is a property of the fixing THREAD, not of the scan. pgbuf_unlatch_void_zone_bcb (src/storage/page_buffer.c:6845) branches on the fixing thread's LRU identity - at :6900-6918 a page goes to the TOP of that thread's PRIVATE list with pgbuf_bcb_register_hit_for_lru(), at :6934 otherwise to the MIDDLE of a round-robin SHARED list where pgbuf_get_victim_from_lru_list() (:9268) reclaims it almost immediately. A pooled parallel-query worker never has an identity: thread_entry_task.cpp:75-76 retire_context() sets private_lru_index = -1 and m_is_private_lru_enabled = false, :95 recycle_context() repeats it, and px_scan_task.cpp:94 propagates m_px_orig_thread_entry = m_parent_thread_p from the parent AND NOTHING ELSE. Only session.c:740 and server_support.c:2401,2437 ever assign one - i.e. the client transaction thread that serves a NO_PARALLEL_SCAN scan. PostgreSQL contrast: heapam.c:398-410 initscan() sets BAS_BULKREAD from rs_nblocks > NBuffers/4, :1340 sets SO_ALLOW_STRAT so each worker's own heap_beginscan builds its own 256 kB ring (freelist.c:426,442), and GetBufferFromRing/AddBufferToRing (:623,:702) recycle only pages the scan itself read - DOP-independent by construction, and StrategyGetBuffer (:184) is 1.73% of PostgreSQL's Q06 profile so the ring is provably active. Effect: 458,209 -> 158,930 reads/statement, -4.57 GiB of page-cache traffic, worth about 1.66 core-s of the 14.023 core-s excess (11.8%), independently bounded by CUBRID's measured 2.500 core-s parallel CPU inflation of which this is 66%. Fix: propagate the parent's private_lru_index at px_scan_task.cpp:94 beside the existing m_px_orig_thread_entry assignment and call the existing pgbuf_thread_variables_init(). LIMITATION recorded: /*+ PARALLEL(1) */ degenerates to the serial non-px path, so the one-pooled-worker control is unobtainable on this build; the mechanism claim rests on the source branch plus the DOP-flat step, and validation criterion 3 (DOP independence restored) is written to settle it.

headline_finding: CUBRID chose the wrong plan. Both engines are faster on the hash shape and slower on the index-nested-loop shape, and CUBRID is the one running the index-nested-loop shape. Q09 is the exact converse of Q08, where F_plan and F_cpu both favoured CUBRID and the loss sat entirely in F_units; here F_units is the smallest factor (1.177424x of a 2.115055x gap).

headline_finding: Q10 is the FIRST query of this campaign where CUBRID's optimizer beats PostgreSQL's and CUBRID still loses. CUBRID natively picks the index-NL chain (orders sscan -> lineitem fk_lineitem_orders -> customer PK, estimated cost 649494) and is right: its own hash alternative /*+ USE_HASH(lineitem, customer) */ measures 13.809/13.869 s (1.94x slower, cost 9,427,968), and PostgreSQL forced onto CUBRID's shape with enable_hashjoin=off, enable_mergejoin=off gets 1.6979x FASTER (4.218695 -> 2.484120 s). CLASS: structural absence. CUBRID returns degree 1 BEFORE compute_parallel_degree is even evaluated. (2) STRATEGY FLIP ON A HARDCODED CONSTANT - CUBRID query_executor.c:134 `#define HASH_AGGREGATE_VH_SELECTIVITY_THRESHOLD 0.5f`, :131 tuple threshold 2000, decision at :4838-4849 setting context->state = HS_REJECT_ALL permanently, latched at :4648; vs PostgreSQL src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c:1866 hash_agg_check_limits() which tests only MemoryContextMemAllocated against hash_mem_limit and hash_ngroups_current against hash_ngroups_limit - NO selectivity term exists - and on breach calls hash_agg_enter_spill_mode() (:1907) / hashagg_spill_tuple() (:3029), keeping resident groups aggregating and reprocessing spilled partitions at :2734 agg_refill_hash_table(). CLASS: structural absence. PostgreSQL never flips strategy; it degrades by spilling. (3) THE COUNTER THE HEURISTIC READS IS INFLATED - CUBRID query_executor.c:4740-4741 increments group_count on every insert, against the eviction loop at :4808-4835 which adjusts hash_size twice and calls mht_rem but NEVER decrements group_count; vs PostgreSQL nodeAgg.c:1861 hash_ngroups_current, maintained as groups CURRENTLY RESIDENT (incremented at :3243, reset at :2814) so it cannot drift above truth. IMP-018's reproduction from a cold pool was NOT executed: proving that connection 1 on a freshly started server measures 3.544 s again would require stopping and restarting the campaign server, which destroys the state every other Q11 stage was measured in. It is recorded as validation criterion (2) instead. The within-session evidence is already a direct A/B in both directions (three traces, two probes, twelve blocks).

IMP-009's Q11 contribution is a PROJECTION for the CUBRID side: the executed A/B (1.091149x) is on PostgreSQL. A CUBRID-side A/B would need a way to parallelise an uncorrelated subquery, which the pinned tree hardcodes to degree 1. IMP-009's direct CUBRID A/B remains Q05's.

The campaign's WARM protocol has a measured blind spot: SSOT section 12's gate operates on one connection's statement series, and Q11 proves a CUBRID query can pass it (half-split trend -0.16% over 120 statements) while its true steady state is 1.86x faster and reachable only by opening more connections. A candidate strengthening - drive N CONNECTIONS, not N statements, before the contract block - is recorded for later queries. It was NOT applied retroactively and no Q01-Q10 number is restated.

CUBRID's statdump data-page counters remain unusable on this server (second query to confirm it, after Q10). Q11 adds an independent confirmation method (a single-statement bracket against /proc/<pid>/io) and establishes that the LRU/private GAUGES in the same dump ARE reliable.

PostgreSQL's heap_page_prune_opt costs 7.56% of its profile with 9.16% of the profile in asm_exc_page_fault -> handle_mm_fault beneath it, i.e. soft page faults on shared_buffers pages. F_cost is BELOW 1.0 - CUBRID is 1.1017x CHEAPER per page fix - so Q11's CPU factor is a COUNT factor, not a unit-cost factor. Every long-running block driver ran inside its own dedicated child tmux session (q11conv, q11hl, q11plan, q11tel, q11dec, q11fin, q11conn, q11sat, q11perf, q11var, q11probe) per SSOT section 24's tmux-server-survival rule, each polled for its explicit completion marker (DRIVER_EXIT / ALL_BLOCKS_DONE / VARIANT_BLOCKS_DONE / PROBE_DONE / FATAL) and removed once consumed. card_calc.py gained a PRIMARY F_work event of data-page FIXES alongside the existing plan-node-tuple-touch decomposition, because Q11 is page-fix bound and the tuple-touch definition flatters PostgreSQL here (its InitPlan reads all 100,000 supplier rows in one sequential scan, i.e. many tuple touches for very few page fixes). Both are reported, both reconstruct F_cpu exactly, and the tuple-touch version carries its stated bias.

headline_finding: The headline ratio is not the finding. Before Q11 could be measured at all, CUBRID had to be driven through a 2.6408x performance decay that no parameter, plan or query change causes and that SSOT section 12's WARM gate cannot detect: block median 3.544000 -> 1.342000 s while physical page reads per statement fell 566,103 -> 0, with the plan, the query text, every parameter and the page-FIX count all held constant (trace `fetch` 1,012,042 -> 1,012,172 -> 1,011,949, a 0.02% spread). 94.9% of the 1,828 ms recovered is accounted for by the trace's own fetch_time (2,061 -> 528 -> 326 ms). PostgreSQL's number moved 0.01% over the same 22 minutes and ~370 statements: `Buffers: shared hit=676275 read=0` and Execution Time 1079.898 -> 1080.016 ms in three EXPLAIN ANALYZE captures. Two probes separate the variable: ONE connection running 120 statements is FLAT (2.450-2.521 s, half-split trend -0.16%, syscr 193,235-210,348, device read_bytes 0 over 379.9 GiB of rchar), while 60 connections x 4 statements decays 49,292 -> 34,538 -> 18,306 -> 3,519 -> 135 reads/statement over five connections and then holds 111-127 for 55 more, wall 1.581 -> 1.318-1.370 s; and one connection x 60 statements immediately afterwards is FLAT at the new level (median 1.3300 s, spread 2.28%, 96 reads/statement). The decay is CONNECTION-driven. Num_data_page_private_count sits at 5,002 for exactly as long as the misses persist - i.e. at PGBUF_PRIVATE_LRU_MAX_HARD_QUOTA = 5000 (page_buffer.c:1024) - and Num_data_page_lru1 (the shared hot zone) rises 15,092 -> 82,352 -> 97,369, which is Q11's whole working set, when they stop. A single session retains 5,000 of 524,288 pages, 0.95% of an 8,192 MB pool, for a working set that is 18.6% of it.

plan_comparison_summary: The two plans are closer than in any previous query of this campaign, and the join subtree is node-for-node identical. CUBRID (estimated, SET OPTIMIZATION LEVEL 514): temp(order by) <- temp(group by) sort 1 asc <- idx-join <- [idx-join <- sscan nation sargs n_name='GERMANY' + iscan supplier index fk_supplier_nation] + iscan partsupp index fk_partsupp_supplier, cost 6892 for the join and 9752 total, final cardinality estimate 320,000 against a true 323,920 (0.9879x - the most accurate estimate CUBRID has produced in this campaign); plus a structurally IDENTICAL second plan for the uncorrelated HAVING subquery. PostgreSQL (EXPLAIN ANALYZE): Sort <- HashAggregate (Planned Partitions 16, Batches 17, Memory Usage 8337kB, Disk Usage 15064kB, Rows Removed by Filter 296089) <- Nested Loop <- [Nested Loop <- Seq Scan nation Filter + Bitmap Heap Scan supplier on idx_fk_supplier_nation, Heap Blocks exact=1872] + Index Scan idx_fk_partsupp_supplier Index Searches 4049 loops=4049; plus InitPlan expr_1 -> Finalize Aggregate -> Gather (Workers Planned 1, Launched 1) -> Partial Aggregate -> Nested Loop <- Hash Join(supplier Parallel Seq Scan of all 100,000 rows, nation) + Index Scan idx_fk_partsupp_supplier. Buffers: shared hit=676275, temp read=1330 written=3103. Same: the nation filter (25 read, 1 kept), the supplier access (4,049 rows through the same FK index, 1 index search each side), the partsupp access (4,049 index searches, 323,920 rows, same index), and the whole cardinality chain 25 -> 1 -> 4,049 -> 323,920 -> 304,774 -> 8,685 which both engines independently confirm. Different: (1) the aggregation - CUBRID sorts (GROUPBY hash: partial, sort: true, 1,516 sort pages, SERIAL, 313 ms), PostgreSQL hashes and spills 17 batches (~200 ms) - and PostgreSQL's choice is the slower one; (2) the HAVING subquery - CUBRID runs SUBQUERY (uncorrelated) as a serial second copy of the whole join in 619 ms of a 1,532 ms statement (40.4%), PostgreSQL runs the same subquery under a Gather with 1 worker in 237 ms and reaches all 100,000 supplier rows with a Parallel Seq Scan instead of an index probe; (3) the join -> aggregation hand-off - CUBRID materialises the 323,920-row result into a temp list file and re-reads it, PostgreSQL passes TupleTableSlots by reference. Variants measured through the same gated section-12 block: CUBRID /*+ NO_HASH_AGGREGATE */ 1.340000 s (identical plan tree cost 9752, identical fetch 1,011,949, hash: partial -> hash: false, still no parallel workers); PostgreSQL enable_hashagg=off 0.739912 s (GroupAggregate over Sort, external merge Disk 8248kB); PostgreSQL max_parallel_workers_per_gather=0 0.870872 s (InitPlan Gather -> plain Aggregate, 237 -> 316.9 ms).
profile_summary: perf is non-headline; both captures attach to verified PID sets (CUBRID cub_server 1612732 with all 26 query worker TIDs inside it; PostgreSQL postmaster 1433696 attached before the client connected, so inherit-on-fork covers leader 2037469 and worker 2037507) with 0 unknown-symbol lines on both sides (1,422 and 1,575 flat lines, 30,207 and 26,138 samples over 30.002 s). Both were taken in the SATURATED state, so neither profile contains any physical-read work - the cleanest like-for-like comparison of the two buffer managers this campaign has produced. CUBRID bands: pgbuf hash lookup + fix/unfix + LRU list surgery 21.07% (pgbuf_fix_release 17.06, pgbuf_unfix 2.45, pgbuf_ordered_fix_release 0.71, pgbuf_ordered_unfix 0.47, pgbuf_set_dirty 0.38); heap record access 15.92% (spage_get_record 4.62, heap_attrinfo_read_dbvalues 4.32, or_mvcc_get_repid_and_flags 3.86, heap_prepare_get_context 1.71); NUMERIC arithmetic 7.26% (float_numeric_db_value_mul 3.17, qdata_evaluate_aggregate_list 1.30, float_numeric_db_value_add 1.06); userspace memmove 6.13%; external sort 5.23% (qfile_compare_partial_sort_record 2.47); DB_VALUE lifecycle 3.71%; libpthread mutex 3.06%; list-file materialisation 2.73%; kernel page-cache copy 0.00% (nothing above the 0.3% cut - the saturated state takes no reads). The call graph resolves pgbuf_fix_release's internals: pgbuf_search_hash_chain 3.86% + pgbuf_search_hash_chain_no_bcb_lock 1.62% = 5.48% of the profile is buffer hash-chain search, plus pgbuf_lockfree_fix_ro 3.77%. PostgreSQL bands: buffer hash lookup + pin/unpin + lwlock 23.72% (hash_search_with_hash_value 12.73, PinBuffer 4.41, LWLockAttemptLock 1.70, LockBufferInternal 0.76, UnpinBufferNoOwner 0.74, GetPrivateRefCountEntrySlow 0.70, LWLockRelease 0.68, StartReadBuffer 0.65); heap/seq scan 8.07% (heap_page_prune_opt 7.56, whose own call graph is 9.16% asm_exc_page_fault -> handle_mm_fault); index/heap fetch + visibility 7.08% (heap_hot_search_buffer 6.01); numeric arithmetic 6.99% (make_result_safe 2.05, init_var_from_num 1.46, mul_var 1.07); kernel mm / temp file 6.80% (_compound_head 3.82) plus unbanded next_uptodate_folio 5.39 and filemap_map_pages 1.52 from the 17-batch spill's mapping path; palloc 6.71%; hash aggregate build/probe 3.80%; expression interpreter 2.47%; tuple deform 2.24%. IMPORTANT CORRECTION the call graph forced: hash_search_with_hash_value 12.73% is NOT the HashAggregate - 13.41% of its 13.62% inclusive resolves through StartReadBuffer -> PinBufferForBlock -> BufferAlloc -> BufTableLookup, i.e. it is PostgreSQL's SHARED BUFFER hash table, the exact counterpart of CUBRID's pgbuf_search_hash_chain. The naive flat-profile reading would have produced a false 15.38%-vs-1.66% 'CUBRID's buffer manager is 10x heavier' claim. Corrected: the buffer bands are CUBRID 24.13% (21.07% + 3.06% libpthread) vs PostgreSQL 23.72% - equal to 1.017x - on 1,011,949 vs 676,275 page fixes, so per fix CUBRID spends 1339.0 ns of total query CPU against PostgreSQL's 1475.2 ns and is 1.1017x CHEAPER. perf stat: CUBRID 86.047 G cycles @ 2.873 GHz, 141.849 G instructions, IPC 1.65, task-clock 0.998 CPUs (U 1.00965, -1.2%), 39,935 context switches = 1.334 K/s; PostgreSQL 114.577 G cycles, 159.126 G instructions, IPC 1.39, 1.329 CPUs (U 1.24996, +6.3%), 349 context switches = 8.75/s (a 152x rate difference). Per statement 6.345 G vs 4.233 G instructions = 1.4988x, which matches F_work 1.496357x to 0.16% - CUBRID retires 1.50x the instructions because it performs 1.50x the page fixes, at a HIGHER IPC. Q11 is emphatically not a memory-stall story.
rejected_explanations: Each with the number that rejected it. 'CUBRID chose the wrong plan' - the join subtree is node-for-node, index-for-index and probe-count-for-probe-count identical (Index Searches 1 then 4049 on each side), and the only differing decision, the aggregation strategy, is one PostgreSQL gets WRONG: enable_hashagg=off makes PostgreSQL 1.0787x faster, so anchor A's F_plan is 0.927064x, below 1. 'The working set does not fit CUBRID's 8 GiB buffer' (IMP-002's premise) - the set is ~97,400 of 524,288 pages, 18.6% of the pool, and the saturated state takes 0 reads, 0 device read_bytes and 96 read syscalls per statement; it fits 5.4x over. 'Then the misses are unavoidable' - 566,103 -> 0 reads per statement on the same plan with the same 1,012,000 page fixes, with no parameter change, no restart and no query change. 'The decay is just the query getting warmer with more statements' - 120 statements on ONE connection are flat (half-split trend -0.16%, syscr 193k-210k); five CONNECTIONS move it from 49,292 to 135 reads. 'CUBRID's serial group-by sort is the tail' (IMP-015) - /*+ NO_HASH_AGGREGATE */ measures 1.340000 s against 1.342000 s, F_plan 1.001493x inside the 1.28% band, with an identical plan tree (cost 9752), an identical fetch count (1,011,949) and identical rows, and no parallel workers on GROUPBY in either case: at 1,516 sort pages (Q10 had 75,893) compute_parallel_degree returns 1 with or without the veto. 'The 0.5f hash-aggregate abort fired wrongly again' (IMP-016) - measured true selectivity 1.000000 at 2,000 tuples, 1.000000 at 5,040, 1.000000 at 20,000, 0.968610 at 200,000 and 0.940893 over the whole 323,920-tuple input, identical on both engines: HS_REJECT_ALL is CORRECT on Q11. 'max_agg_hash_size is the constraint' (IMP-017) - hashing is abandoned on the FIRST evaluation of a ratio that is exactly 1.000000, so the eviction loop the frozen-static defect lives in never runs. 'CUBRID's buffer manager is more expensive per page' (IMP-013) - with zero misses on both sides the bands are 24.13% vs 23.72% (1.017x) and per fix CUBRID spends 1339.0 ns against 1475.2 ns, 1.1017x CHEAPER; this required correcting the flat profile, since hash_search_with_hash_value 12.73% is BufTableLookup. 'It is a memory-stall / cache-locality difference' - CUBRID's IPC is 1.65 against PostgreSQL's 1.39, i.e. CUBRID stalls LESS; the gap is 1.4988x the instructions, matching F_work 1.496357x to 0.16%. 'CUBRID's parallel-scan degree saturates below the cap' (IMP-012) and 'the parallel-worker private-LRU bypass explains the misses' (IMP-010) - Q11 launches NO parallel units at all (U 1.00965, TWU 0.9975, no `parallel workers` sub-line anywhere), so neither mechanism can fire; Q11's pages DO reach the private list correctly, the list is simply capped. 'The NUMERIC accumulator is the cost' (IMP-001) - 7.26% vs 6.99%, parity at 1.039x. 'The trace's row counters are inflated so F_work is wrong' (IMP-005) - every Q11 counter is exact against ground truth (partsupp 323,920 = G3, supplier 4,049 = G2, GROUPBY 8,685 = G5, nation 25) at scan depth 3, the depth at which Q08/Q10 saw ~2x inflation, which sharpens IMP-005 from 'depth' to 'parallel scan trace merging'. 'The multi-column FK selectivity product mis-estimates the join' (IMP-014) - Q11's FK indexes are single-column and the final cardinality estimate is 0.9879x of truth.

source_contrast: 8 rows with file:line on both sides. (1) A single session retains only 5,000 buffer pages of a 524,288-page pool: CUBRID page_buffer.c:1024 `#define PGBUF_PRIVATE_LRU_MAX_HARD_QUOTA 5000`, applied at :14379 `new_quota = MIN (new_quota, PGBUF_PRIVATE_LRU_MAX_HARD_QUOTA);`, with a second independent ceiling at :14193 `#define MIN_PRIVATE_RATIO 0.01f` feeding :14363 `all_private_quota = (int) ((pgbuf_Pool.num_buffers - ...invalid_cnt) * quota->private_pages_ratio)` = 0.01 * 524,288 = 5,242 -- both ceilings coincide within 9% on this pool size, so the measurement CANNOT separate them and both must change; vs PostgreSQL freelist.c:184 `StrategyGetBuffer(BufferAccessStrategy strategy, ...)` where a ring is consulted only `if (strategy != NULL)` and otherwise a clock sweep runs over the whole NBuffers, with no per-backend/per-session/per-connection budget anywhere in the file. STRUCTURAL ABSENCE. (2) Every page a serial query reads goes on the SESSION's private list: CUBRID page_buffer.c:6902-6912 pgbuf_unlatch_void_zone_bcb() `if (thread_private_lru_index != -1) { ... pgbuf_lru_add_new_bcb_to_top (thread_p, bcb, thread_private_lru_index); ... }` with :206 documenting PGBUF_VOID_ZONE as the zone every physically read page passes through; vs PostgreSQL bufmgr.c:926 `ReadBufferExtended(reln, forkNum, blockNum, RBM_NORMAL, NULL)` (an index scan passes strategy = NULL) and bufmgr.c:3335-3341 `if (strategy == NULL) { /* Default case: increase usagecount unless already max. */ ... buf_state += BUF_USAGECOUNT_ONE; }`. STRUCTURAL ABSENCE. (3) The escape from the private list is unreachable for a scan pattern: CUBRID page_buffer.c:6951-6984 pgbuf_should_move_private_to_shared() -- cond 1 `thread_private_lru_index != bcb_lru_idx` (another session), cond 2 `pgbuf_bcb_is_hot(bcb)` AND `PGBUF_IS_BCB_OLD_ENOUGH` -- with :106 `#define PGBUF_FIX_COUNT_THRESHOLD 64` tested at :16294, against Q11's measured 3.47 fixes per page per statement inside a 5,000-page window over a 93,281-page heap; vs PostgreSQL freelist.c:442 `case BAS_BULKREAD:` (256 kB ring) and :755 `if (strategy->btype != BAS_BULKREAD)` -- PostgreSQL HAS a small-window mode but it is OPT-IN for large sequential scans and nothing demotes a default-strategy page into a smaller window. STRUCTURAL ABSENCE. (4) The one operator control cannot be changed on a running server: CUBRID system_parameter.c:4168-4175 PRM_ID_PB_NUM_PRIVATE_CHAINS `"num_private_chains"`, `(PRM_FOR_SERVER | PRM_RELOADABLE)`, `PRM_CLEAR_DYNAMIC_FLAG`; vs PostgreSQL freelist.c:511 `GetAccessStrategyWithSize(btype, ring_size_kb)` where the window is a per-scan argument. STRUCTURAL ABSENCE. (5) The uncorrelated HAVING subquery cannot use more than one unit: CUBRID px_parallel.cpp:85-109 compute_parallel_degree() `case parallel_type::SUBQUERY`, :89-92 `/* TODO: degree fixed at 1 (main + gather) */` (IMP-009); vs PostgreSQL's InitPlan generation placing the uncorrelated aggregate under a normal Gather, executed as `Workers Planned: 1, Workers Launched: 1` with loops=2 beneath it. Measured: 619 ms serial vs 237 ms at 2 units, and removing that worker costs PostgreSQL 1.091149x. STRUCTURAL ABSENCE. (6) The join result is materialised into a temp list file and the aggregation's page traffic goes through the buffer manager: CUBRID query_executor.c:1255-1259 qexec_end_one_iteration() and list_file.c:1851 qfile_generate_tuple_into_list (IMP-006), 2.73% self plus the 331,691 page fixes it causes; vs PostgreSQL nodeAgg.c consuming its outer Nested Loop's TupleTableSlot by reference and hashagg_spill_tuple (:3029) spilling to a TEMP FILE outside the buffer manager (`temp read=1330 written=3103`, shared hit unchanged). 331,691 of CUBRID's 1,011,949 fixes (32.8%) are the aggregation's, against 0 for PostgreSQL's; CUBRID's join subtree alone (680,258) is within 0.6% of PostgreSQL's entire total. SAME STAGE, LOWER MEASURED COST. headline_finding: Q12 looks like a parallelism story and is not, and the measurement - not an argument - is what refutes it. A 10,671 MiB single-table scan where PostgreSQL prints 'Workers Planned: 5' and CUBRID's plan text prints nothing invites the conclusion that CUBRID runs it serially. CUBRID runs SIX parallel heap-scan workers (trace: 'parallel workers: 6', per-worker readrows 9,938,887..10,011,920 summing to 59,986,052), because px_scan.cpp:416 auto-derives the degree from the relation's page count at EXECUTION time, which is why no plan annotation exists. Measured through each engine's own switch in the same gated section-12 block, CUBRID's parallel implementation is the BETTER one: 5.3570x speedup for a 1.0971x CPU surcharge and 91.9% parallel efficiency against PostgreSQL's 4.9994x, 1.1733x and 77.0%. And the gap is LARGER at one unit than at six - serial 21.636999/13.098051 = 1.65193x versus parallel 1.541648x - so parallelism NARROWS Q12's gap by 6.7%. Where the 1.54x actually lives, from a 333,064-sample profile with 0 unresolved symbols and an empty unbanded remainder: per-row attribute materialisation into DB_VALUEs is +3.2854 core-s and the per-value lifecycle PostgreSQL does not have at all is +1.4219 core-s, together 69.5% of the 6.7771 core-s CPU excess. CUBRID spends 27.31 ns of total query CPU per attribute materialised against PostgreSQL's 5.45 ns - 5.01x - while materialising THREE TIMES FEWER attributes (5 per row against 15, because PostgreSQL must deform up to l_shipmode, attribute 15 of lineitem's 16). perf stat confirms it is instruction count and not stalling: 2,493 instructions per row against 1,398 at a HIGHER IPC, 2.32 against 1.99. Two profile bands go the OTHER way: CUBRID's predicate evaluation is 0.913x and its B-tree descent 0.424x, both cheaper in absolute core-seconds than PostgreSQL's.

plan_comparison_summary: Structurally identical, operator for operator, which is why F_plan is 1.0000 by structural equality rather than by an anchor. CUBRID (SET OPTIMIZATION LEVEL 514, non-executing): temp(group by) over subplan idx-join(inner) with outer sscan on lineitem carrying all four predicates as sargs (cost 832902 card 23711) and inner iscan on pk_orders_o_orderkey (cost 4), then sort 1 asc, total cost 845161 card 10114. PostgreSQL (EXPLAIN ANALYZE BUFFERS VERBOSE SETTINGS): Finalize GroupAggregate <- Gather Merge (Workers Planned 5, Launched 5) <- Partial GroupAggregate <- Sort (quicksort, 3792 kB) <- Nested Loop (Inner Unique: true) <- Parallel Seq Scan on lineitem (Rows Removed by Filter 9,945,875 x 6 loops) + Index Scan using orders_pkey (310,803 searches), Execution Time 2673.156 ms. Stage by stage: driving access = full heap scan with pushed-down residual filter on both; join = index-nested-loop on both; inner = the same unique PK index on both; direction = lineitem outer on both; grouping = sort-based on both; ordering = l_shipmode ascending on both; units = 6 on both. The two counters that would betray a hidden shape difference agree: index probes 310,803 vs 310,430-310,732 (0.12% apart, the shortfall being IMP-005's merge defect) and index-side page fixes 1,109,634 vs 1,105,561 (0.37%). Two controlled variants confirm neither native plan is an artifact of the unit count: the operator chain is unchanged at 1 unit and at 6 on both engines.

(4) 'The generic DB_VALUE comparator (IMP-008) loses Q12' - REJECTED by the profile: band C is 4.5391 core-s CUBRID against 4.9697 PostgreSQL, 0.913x, CUBRID CHEAPER, at 39.1 ns per term evaluation against 54.3 ns, while doing 1.1605x MORE evaluations. headline_finding:
Q13 is the cleanest comparison in the campaign so far and the least ambiguous finding, because almost everything that usually confounds these numbers is provably absent.

Both engines take ZERO physical reads (read_bytes 0 on both, Num_data_page_ioreads delta 0, pg_stat_database.blks_read delta 0). Both choose the SAME join: an index nested loop with customer as outer and orders probed through the FK index. Both produce the SAME 15,337,604 join rows, verified by ten ground-truth cardinalities that agree exactly on both engines. Both fix the same number of pages at the matched node: CUBRID trace fetch 19,504,609 against PostgreSQL Buffers: shared hit=19,499,552, a ratio of 1.000259x. So F_work is exactly 1.000000 and the ENTIRE 2.246313x is cost per unit of identical work.

Nearly half of that cost is ONE FUNCTION. The UTF-8 LIKE matcher for o_comment not like '%special%requests%' -- evaluated 15,000,000 times per statement -- is 33.01% of CUBRID's CPU (15.995 core-s per statement) against PostgreSQL's 12.57% (2.773 core-s). Under two deliberately different band bracketings it is 46.4%-47.8% of the whole 26.3964 core-s per-statement CPU gap, at a 4.27x-5.55x band ratio.

Charset and collation parity was verified BEFORE that band was attributed, because the obvious objection is that PostgreSQL might be on a byte path. It is not: the database is encoding UTF8, so like.c:156-161 routes to UTF8_MatchText rather than the single-byte SB_MatchText, and CUBRID's column is COLLATE utf8_bin. Both engines run a UTF-8, deterministic, binary-ordering LIKE over the same bytes.

The second finding is an optimizer defect, new to this campaign (IMP-021). CUBRID cannot use an index scan whose only value is the ordering it supplies whenever the query contains a join, so it materialises all 15,337,604 join rows into a 326 MiB temp file and sorts them to satisfy GROUP BY c_custkey, while PostgreSQL streams the same grouping off a Parallel Index Only Scan with no Sort node anywhere in its plan.

What Q13 is NOT, each rejected with a number: not parallelism (F_units 1.029635x); not I/O (zero physical reads, parallel vs serial page fixes 0.00067% apart); not a memory stall (CUBRID's IPC is 1.73 against PostgreSQL's 1.19 -- it simply retires 3.1220x the instructions); and not 'PostgreSQL's executor is better', because denying PostgreSQL its ordered parallel path makes it take 13.678 s, i.e. CUBRID is 1.1972x FASTER on the shape CUBRID is confined to.

IMP-004.correctness_risk: Medium-to-high. This path implements LIKE semantics for every collation, including contraction and UCA-level collations (lang_strmatch_utf8_w_contr, lang_strmatch_utf8_uca_w_level) and case-insensitive collations. The fast path must be gated so any non-deterministic collation, contraction table, case-insensitive collation, trailing-space rule or non-ASCII byte falls back to the existing loop.

The predicate 'o_comment not like ''%special%requests%''' is evaluated 15,000,000 times per statement (trace btree rows: 15000000, lookup rows: 14837583, difference 162,417 = ground truth G2). TWO NEW SOURCE FACTS: (a) intl_utf8_to_cp@plt and intl_nextchar_utf8@plt appear as separate PLT symbols, proving the per-character decode is genuinely not inlined; (b) language_support.c:2843-2846 shows the only collation-dependent branch inside the matcher selects a different WEIGHT TABLE, never a different algorithm, so utf8_bin -- whose weight function is the identity -- still pays two intl_utf8_to_cp decodes (:2857,:2858) and two weight-table lookups (:2877,:2893) per character. PostgreSQL's advantage is the UTF-8 specialization at like.c:128-134 (NextChar = pointer increment + continuation-byte test, no decode, no table, no call) plus the one-byte candidate rejection at like_match.c:174-185. RECOMMEND RAISING TO P0 at the next ledger review on this evidence.
IMP-004.mechanism_cubrid: lang_strmatch_utf8() advances one character at a time and per position calls intl_utf8_to_cp() on both the target and the pattern, then maps each resulting codepoint through the collation weight table before comparing. There is no ASCII fast path and no byte-lockstep comparison, so a pure-ASCII pattern against an ASCII column still pays two codepoint decodes plus two table lookups per character. The profile shows both decode helpers reached through the dynamic linker on every character: intl_utf8_to_cp 4.82% + @plt 1.75%, intl_nextchar_utf8 3.09% + @plt 1.07% - 2.82% of total query CPU is PLT stub overhead alone.
IMP-004.mechanism_postgresql: MatchText() documents and implements byte-by-byte comparison even for multi-byte encodings, on the grounds that text and pattern stay in lockstep outside wildcard handling, and advances characters with a two-instruction inline macro that just skips UTF-8 continuation bytes. No codepoint is materialized, no weight table is consulted, and there is no out-of-line call in the inner loop.

(3) Same slice with a PARALLEL outer scan forced by c_custkey-0<5000 (q3-doubling-parallel-trace.out): depth 2 still exact (readkeys 1,079, rows 11,054, lookups 5,422) while depth 3 is exactly 2x (readkeys 10,844, rows 43,694, lookups 2,112).

(5) Q04 NEGATIVE CONTROL - no duplication, every counter exact under a 6-worker parallel outer scan:
orders scan readrows reported 15,000,000 vs true cardinality 15,000,000; correlated-subquery readkeys reported 573,671 vs true probe count 573,671 (q4-groundtruth-{cubrid,pg}.out, identical on both engines); lookup rows reported 526,040 vs true answer row count 526,040.
WHY: Q04's XASL hangs the correlated EXISTS subquery off the ROOT node's dptr_list and has NO scan_ptr chain (single-table driving scan, no nested-loop join). merge_xasl_tree() therefore merges it exactly once at src/query/parallel/px_scan/px_scan_trace_handler.cpp:467-470, and the duplicating loop at :493-500 never executes because xasl_tree->scan_ptr is nullptr.
WHAT THIS PINS: this is the negative control the Q03 entry asked for. It SCOPES the defect - the (depth-1) multiplication requires a non-empty scan_ptr chain, so a correlated subquery under the root is unaffected - and it pins the root-dptr merge path with exact numbers a fix must preserve. It does NOT clear the :496-499 inner dptr_list loop, which merges a dptr hanging off a scan_ptr LEVEL and is still double-counted by construction, because the outer xasl_merge_stats(xptr1) has already recursed into xptr1's dptr_list via iterate_xasl_tree (src/xasl/xasl_iteration.hpp:180-187, called from src/xasl/xasl_iteration.cpp:205); Q04 simply does not exercise it.
Raw: q4-trace-cubrid.out, q4-groundtruth-cubrid.out, q4-groundtruth-pg.out.

Q13: new instance on a new plan shape. q13-trace-cubrid.out reports 'ORDERBY (time: 0, sort: true, page: 20861, ioread: 0)' for a 46-ROW sort; 20,861 is the inner GROUPBY node's temp page count re-reported at an ancestor node. Excluded from every calculation in the Q13 report.
IMP-005.mechanism_cubrid: Each parallel worker executes a private clone of the sub-plan below the parallel scan. When a worker finishes, merge_xasl_tree() folds its XASL clone into the coordinator's tree. For the nested-loop chain it iterates the scan_ptr list and calls xasl_merge_stats(xptr1, main) for every level. xasl_merge_stats does not merge a single node: its last statement is iterate_xasl_tree(src, merge_stats, true), which recurses through scan_ptr (xasl_iteration.hpp:189-191) and merges every node in the subtree by header.id with +=. So the level-2 node is merged once (from the caller's first iteration), the level-3 node twice (once inside level-2's subtree walk, once from the caller's second iteration), the level-4 node three times, and a level-k node (k-1) times. The output row counts, and therefore query results, are unaffected - only the trace counters are.
IMP-005.mechanism_postgresql: PostgreSQL keeps a per-worker NodeInstrumentation array in DSM and merges it with planstate_tree_walker (execParallel.c:1173), which visits every PlanState exactly once; for the node being visited it loops over the worker slots and calls InstrAggNode once per worker (execParallel.c:1115). The merge primitive itself (instrument.c:232) touches only the node handed to it and never re-walks children, so no node can be visited by two overlapping traversals.
postgresql_source: src/backend/executor/execParallel.c:1094 ExecParallelRetrieveInstrumentation()
src/backend/executor/execParallel.c:1115 InstrAggNode(planstate->instrument, &instrument[n]) - aggregates each worker's slot exactly once for the node currently being visited

src/backend/executor/execParallel.c:1173 planstate_tree_walker(planstate, ExecParallelRetrieveInstrumentation, ...) - the walker visits each plan node exactly once and the per-node merge does not itself re-walk the subtree
src/backend/executor/instrument.c:232 InstrAggNode() - the additive merge primitive, called once per (node, worker) pair
IMP-005.priority_justification: No runtime cost, but it corrupts the primary evidence source for every parallel nested-loop plan by an exact integer factor: Q03's own W_C would have been overstated by 5,845,603 index entries and 302,114 heap lookups (a 1.54x error on W_C_native) had the doubling not been caught and corrected.

q05_relation.consequence: this is a direct dependency between two candidates: fixing IMP-009 raises this chain's degree above 1 and would expose Q05's five-level chain to the IMP-005 multiplication for the first time. IMP-005 must be fixed first or validated together with IMP-009.
q05_relation.finding: Q05 has the deepest scan_ptr chain in the campaign so far - five nested index scans (region -> nation -> customer -> orders -> lineitem) - which by the (k-1)x rule should overstate the level-5 counters by 4x. q06_evidence.defect_2_impact: A user reading a parallel Q06 trace cannot tell that 98.1% of the scanned rows were discarded by the sargs, which is precisely the number needed to judge whether an index would help. It is an observability defect with no runtime cost.
q06_evidence.defect_2_rows_counter: For the identical query and identical result, the serial trace reports the scan's output correctly as 'rows: 1139264' while every parallel trace reports 'rows: 59986052' - the READROWS value, i.e. the qualified-row counter is overwritten by the scanned-row counter on the parallel gather path. Evidence: variants/trace-NOPARALLELSCAN.txt and variants/trace-PARALLEL1.txt both show readrows 59986052 / rows 1139264; q6-trace-cubrid.out (6 workers), variants/trace-PARALLEL3.txt and variants/trace-PARALLEL12.txt all show readrows 59986052 / rows 59986052. Ground truth is 1,139,264, confirmed identically on both engines by count(*) (q6-groundtruth-cubrid.out, q6-groundtruth-pg.out) and by PostgreSQL's own actual plan (rows=189877.33 loops=6 = 1,139,264 with 'Rows Removed by Filter: 9807798' x 6 = 58,846,788; 1,139,264 + 58,846,788 = 59,986,052 exactly).
q06_evidence.defect_3_statdump_counters: The server-global page-buffer counters do not advance at all for the parallel scan path: cubrid statdump reported Num_data_page_fetches = 23,255,736, Num_data_page_ioreads = 814,716 and Data_page_buffer_hit_ratio = 96.49 both BEFORE and AFTER a statement that provably issued 608,635 pread syscalls totalling 9.29 GiB (/proc/<cub_server>/io syscr and rchar deltas, q6-cubrid-bufstate.txt). Two consecutive invocations returned byte-identical values including Num_data_page_hash_anchor_waits. All of Q06's buffer evidence therefore rests on the trace counters plus /proc/<pid>/io, and statdump's page gauges are recorded as UNRELIABLE for this campaign.
q06_evidence.original_defect_control: Q06's scan_ptr chain is depth 1, so the documented (k-1)x multiplication predicts an exact counter, and the trace's fetch (682,938) and ioread (608,427) match the independently measured page count (682,937 heap pages) and syscall count (608,496-608,635) to within 0.03%. Q06 is therefore a POSITIVE control that bounds the original defect to nested chains, complementing Q05's negative control which bounded it to chains that actually get parallel workers.
q06_evidence.summary: Q06 adds a SECOND, mechanically distinct parallel-scan statistics defect in the same subsystem, plus a positive control for the original one.

IMP-005.q08_relation: Q08 is the cleanest demonstration yet, because every trace discrepancy is an EXACT integer multiple of ground truth: lineitem fk_lineitem_partsupp readkeys 67,236 = 13,452 x 5.00 (the worker count); orders pk readkeys 806,974 = 403,487 x 2.00 and orders lookup rows 244,808 = 122,404 x 2.00 (scan_ptr depth 2); customer pk readkeys 367,194 = 122,404 x 3.00 (depth 3); top-level SCAN/GROUPBY rows 24,254 x 1.00. The multiplier equals 1 at the top, the worker count at the driving level and the scan_ptr depth at intermediate levels. Consequence is methodological: Q08's F_work numerator had to be built from ground-truth count(*) queries instead of the trace, and IMP-012's implementation step (a) cannot ship before this is fixed, because moving work onto the coordinator thread adds another merge level.
IMP-005.q09_evidence: Q09: confirmed at a sixth query and extended to depth 6. Trace rows vs ground truth: partsupp depth 2 = 1x (435,128), lineitem depth 3 = exactly 2x (6,523,226 vs 3,261,613), orders depth 4 = exactly 3x (9,784,839), supplier depth 5 = 3.74x (12,197,824, a new off-rule variant), nation depth 6 = exactly 5x (16,308,065 hit+miss). IMP-005.q10_evidence: Q10 (confirmed again, with a cross-engine ground truth for the correct value): the depth-3 scan of the index-NL chain, `SCAN (index: dba.customer.pk_customer_c_custkey)`, reports `readkeys: 2250758, filteredkeys: 2250758, rows: 2250758` and `fetch: 7736050` for an operation whose required count is 1,147,084 - the number of rows that survive the l_returnflag='R' sarg, confirmed by ground truth (G3_orders_join_lineitem_R = 1,147,084 on both engines) and by PostgreSQL executing the byte-identical shape under enable_hashjoin=off, where `Index Scan using customer_pkey ... loops=1147084, Index Searches: 1147084`. q_evidence.Q11: Q11 NEGATIVE CONTROL. Every CUBRID trace row counter on Q11 is EXACT against ground truth that both engines answer identically: partsupp SCAN `rows: 323920` == G3 323,920, supplier SCAN `rows: 4049` == G2 4,049, GROUPBY `rows: 8685` == G5 8,685, nation `readrows: 25` == 25. Q11's scan nest is depth 3 (nation -> supplier -> partsupp), the same depth at which Q08/Q10 saw 1.96x-2x inflation, so the defect is depth-INDEPENDENT in the way IMP-005 currently states it: Q11 runs no parallel scan units (U=1.00965, no `parallel workers` sub-line anywhere in the trace), and xasl_merge_stats' double-merge needs the parallel sibling-XASL path. Q11 therefore sharpens IMP-005: the inflation is a property of PARALLEL scan trace merging, not of nesting depth alone. Q11's F_work is safe to build from trace counters, and it is.
q_evidence.Q12: Q12 adds a second, larger instance of the same parallel-worker statistics defect and extends it from the trace to statdump. Trace side: for the native parallel plan the traced statement reports 'SELECT (fetch: 113)' and 'SCAN (table: dba.lineitem) ... fetch: 44, readrows: 0, rows: 0' on the main thread while statdump's Num_data_page_fetches bracketed around that same statement moves by 1,788,621 -- the SELECT node under-reports page fixes by 15,829x, and readrows is reported as 0 for a scan that read 59,986,052 rows (the per-worker range line '(parallel workers: 6, readrows: 9938887..10011920)' is the only place the real figure appears, and it is a RANGE, not a total). The same statement run with /*+ NO_PARALLEL_SCAN */ reports every field correctly: 'SELECT (fetch: 2608801, ioread: 417881)' matching its statdump delta of 2,608,803 to 2 fixes. Second, new observation: the 4-statement diagnostic block moved Num_data_page_fetches by exactly 0 (106,169,292 -> 106,169,292 across 24 statements) while the single traced statement moved it by 1,788,621, i.e. the server-wide page counters appear to accumulate only while statement-level tracing is active. That is recorded as an OBSERVATION with its evidence, not as a proven mechanism -- the likely gate is perfmon_is_perf_tracking_and_active(), but this campaign did not run the controlled experiment that would prove it, and the practical consequence is only that Q12 used the trace-bracketed statdump deltas and /proc/<cub_server>/io rather than the block-bracketed statdump. raw/Q12/q12-serial-parallel.out, q12-serial-serial.out, q12-serial-statdump-*.txt, Q12-cubrid-buffer-io-diag.json.

IMP-005.ranking_rationale: Ranked below IMP-006 and IMP-007 on runtime effect, which is zero, and above nothing on that axis. It is recorded at P2 rather than P3 because it is a precondition for trusting the other two: Q03's own F_work would have been wrong by 1.54x on the native side if the trace had been believed. It is also the cheapest fix in the registry (a one-loop change) with the lowest risk.

IMP-005.root_cause_title: Parallel-scan trace statistics for a nested-loop subtree are merged once per scan_ptr level and again by the whole-subtree walk inside xasl_merge_stats, so a level-k scan's counters are reported (k-1) times: depth 3 is exactly 2x and depth 4 exactly 3x
IMP-005.upstream_precedent: Yes, same class: 85984d18d [CBRD-26839] 'Emit zero-stats parallel heap scan trace when no worker stats collected' (#7219), 2be90e6dd [CBRD-26704] 'Modify trace results to be hidden when Correlated subquery cache is not used' (#7043) and 34fc7779a [CBRD-26681] 'Exclude memoize trace results from output when Memoize is not used' (#7018) are all parallel-scan trace-output correctness fixes in the same subsystem, and all are ancestors of the pinned build. The defect itself was introduced by 0c6088ab3 [CBRD-26722] (#7062).
IMP-005.validation_criteria: (1) q3-doubling-parallel-trace.out reports depth-3 readkeys 5,422, rows 21,847, lookups 1,056 - byte-equal to the serial control q3-doubling-trace.out; (2) the depth-4 probe reports partsupp 8,905, not 26,715; (3) Q03's full trace reports lineitem entries 5,845,603 and lookups 302,114, matching PostgreSQL's 302,114; (4) MEMOIZE and SUBQUERY_CACHE hit/miss and the sq_cache totals are unchanged on the Q02 correlated-subquery trace, proving the dptr path was not broken; (5) no change to any query result or headline timing. (6) Q04 REGRESSION PIN, added from the Q04 negative control: after the fix, Q04's trace must still report orders readrows 15,000,000, subquery readkeys 573,671 and lookup rows 526,040 exactly, proving the root-dptr merge path (px_scan_trace_handler.cpp:467-470) was not broken while the scan_ptr double traversal was removed.

IMP-010.correctness_risk: Low for the insertion-point variants: LRU placement is a performance policy and cannot change query results, and the buffer's own latching/pinning is untouched. The real risks are operational rather than semantic: (a) sharing one private LRU list across N workers concentrates list-mutation traffic on one lock, so it must be measured for contention at high DOP, and the fallback variant above exists for exactly that outcome; (b) a private list that now legitimately holds the whole pool must not starve other sessions, so pgbuf_adjust_quotas' behaviour under a single large private consumer needs checking - note that the SERIAL path already produces exactly this state today, so it is a state the pool demonstrably tolerates.

IMP-010.difficulty_reason: The primary fix is propagating two existing fields at one existing propagation site (px_scan_task.cpp:94) plus a call to the existing pgbuf_thread_variables_init(); no new mechanism, no data structure change, no plan or semantic change. Difficulty rises to medium only if the private-list contention fallback is needed, and to high for the structurally clean per-scan-strategy redesign recorded as the alternative.
IMP-010.effect_range: Direct A/B: removing the amplification takes CUBRID from 458,209 to 158,930 physical page reads per statement, i.e. -4.57 GiB of page-cache traffic. If the kernel read band scales with bytes, the 2.543 core-s band falls to about 0.882 core-s, releasing roughly 1.66 core-s of the 14.023 core-s Q06 CPU excess (11.8%). That is also 66% of CUBRID's measured 2.500 core-s parallel CPU inflation (20.629 core-s serial -> 23.128 core-s at 6 units), which is the independent upper bound. No wall claim is made beyond that: at 5.97 active units a CPU saving converts to wall only in proportion to utilization, so the expected wall gain is about 0.28 s of 3.875 s. On a host where the data did NOT fit the OS page cache the same 4.57 GiB would be device I/O and the effect would be far larger; this campaign's host makes Q06 the CHEAP case, not the expensive one.
IMP-010.evidence_event: physical page reads per statement for one full scan of the same relation in the same pool, as a function of nothing but the number of scan units. Denominator: lineitem = 682,937 CUBRID heap pages of 16 KiB in a 524,288-page (8 GiB) pool, so the arithmetically unavoidable overflow is 682,937 - 524,288 = 158,649 pages per statement. Measured by /proc/<cub_server>/io syscr deltas divided by the statement count, cross-checked against the trace's own ioread counter.
IMP-010.explanation: One scan thread reads 158,930 pages per statement - the predicted overflow to within 0.18% - so CUBRID's replacement policy retains the entire pool's worth of the relation and behaves optimally. The identical scan on 3, 6 or 12 pooled workers reads 468,980 / 458,209 / 459,242 pages, retaining only 213,957-224,728, and the degradation is flat in DOP rather than proportional to it: it is a step change caused by WHICH LRU list receives the pages, not by concurrency pressure. PostgreSQL, whose scan-resistance is a per-scan strategy ring rather than a per-thread list, reads 76,987 pages serially and 78,482 at DOP 5 against a predicted overflow of 76,552 - a 1.9% DOP effect against CUBRID's 188%.
IMP-010.implementation_direction: Propagate the parent's LRU identity into the parallel-scan worker's thread entry at src/query/parallel/px_scan/px_scan_task.cpp:94, next to the existing m_px_orig_thread_entry assignment: copy m_parent_thread_p->private_lru_index and call pgbuf_thread_variables_init() so m_is_private_lru_enabled follows, and clear both again on retire (thread_entry_task.cpp:75-76 already does). All N workers of one scan then share the ONE private list of the session that owns the query, which is the same list the serial path uses, so the serial retention behaviour is reproduced exactly rather than approximated. Cheaper and less invasive alternative if sharing one private list across workers proves contended: keep the shared list but insert scan pages at the TOP rather than the MIDDLE when the fixing thread is a parallel-scan worker of a sequential scan; that recovers most of the retention without touching thread identity. The structurally cleanest fix - and the one PostgreSQL's design argues for - is to make scan-resistance a property of the SCAN (a per-scan ring/strategy handed to pgbuf_fix, as in freelist.c:426) instead of a property of the fixing thread, which removes the whole class of defect rather than this instance.

measurement.kernel_read_band_call_graph: pgbuf_ordered_fix_release -> pgbuf_fix_release -> pgbuf_claim_bcb_for_fix -> fileio_read -> __libc_pread64 -> vfs_read -> xfs_file_buffered_read -> filemap_read -> copy_page_to_iter -> rep_movs_alternative (9.18%)
measurement.limitation_no_single_worker_control: The cleanest possible control - one POOLED worker, which would separate 'which thread fixes the page' from 'how many threads contend' - is not obtainable on this build: /*+ PARALLEL(1) */ degenerates to the serial non-px path (variants/trace-PARALLEL1.txt shows no 'parallel workers' line, reports rows: 1139264 correctly, and reads 158,929 pages, all identical to NO_PARALLEL_SCAN). The mechanism claim therefore rests on (a) the source branch at page_buffer.c:6900-6934 together with thread_entry_task.cpp:75-76,95 and px_scan_task.cpp:94, and (b) the measurement being a STEP at >=2 workers that is then flat across DOP 3, 6 and 12 rather than scaling with worker count. A contention explanation predicts DOP dependence and is rejected by that flatness; it is not excluded by a single-worker control, and that gap is recorded rather than glossed. The validation criteria above are written so that applying the fix settles it either way.
measurement.pool_state_dependence: The parallel read count is itself unstable across pool states while the serial one is not: the three headline-regime telemetry blocks all measured 608,510 reads per statement (rchar 39,874,595,032-096 bytes per 4-statement block, i.e. 89.1% miss) while the lru_ab probe, which drives each variant to its own equilibrium with two extra passes first, measured 458,209-468,980 across DOP 3/6/12 (67.1-68.7%). Serial measured 158,930 and 162,257 in the same two settings (23.27% and 23.76%). Read amplification is therefore 2.88x-3.83x depending on pool state, and the section 12 headline regime sits at the 3.83x end. That the PARALLEL figure wobbles by 33% while the SERIAL figure is pinned to the arithmetic overflow is additional evidence that the parallel path's retention is unstable, not merely lower.

measurement: Q13: NEGATIVE result, recorded as a SCOPE BOUND rather than as confirming evidence. A controlled traced parallel statement and a traced /*+ NO_PARALLEL_SCAN */ statement, each bracketed by /proc/<cub_server>/io and statdump, give Num_data_page_fetches of 22,649,042 vs 22,648,891 -- 0.00067% apart -- with read_bytes 0 on both. IMP-010's damage mechanism is re-reading pages the parallel path evicted; Q13's working set is resident in the 8192 MB pool so there is nothing to re-read. This narrows IMP-010 to the working-set-exceeds-pool regime; it does not weaken the finding.

IMP-010.priority_justification: 2.883x measured physical-read amplification with a same-engine, same-query, same-pool A/B and a source path localized to one propagation site, worth about 1.66 core-s of Q06's 14.023 core-s CPU excess (11.8%). Not P0 because on THIS host every one of those reads is served by the OS page cache (device read_bytes delta 0), so the wall effect is only about 0.28 s of 3.875 s; the P0 case would be a host where the working set does not fit RAM, which this campaign does not measure and therefore does not claim. Ranked above IMP-007 because it removes 65% of the reads instead of making each cheaper, and because it is a one-site fix rather than an I/O-path redesign.

q_evidence.Q12: Q12 extends IMP-010 from SELF-eviction to COLLATERAL eviction, which is a qualitatively new consequence of the same root cause. Q06 measured the parallel scan re-reading the relation IT WAS SCANNING; Q12 measures it evicting a DIFFERENT relation -- the inner side of its own index-nested-loop join. Direct same-engine A/B on one traced statement each, /proc/<cub_server>/io bracketed: PARALLEL 613,666 read syscalls and 9.361 GiB, SERIAL /*+ NO_PARALLEL_SCAN */ 418,246 and 6.376 GiB -- the parallel path adds 195,420 reads and 2.985 GiB per statement (+46.7%), cross-checked by statdump Num_data_page_ioreads 613,460 vs 417,882. The collateral part is the decisive number: CUBRID's trace charges 100,930-117,883 of those reads to the orders PK index+heap SCAN node (two traced runs, pool-state dependent), while PostgreSQL's EXPLAIN ANALYZE reports 'Index Scan using orders_pkey ... Buffers: shared hit=1109634' with read=0 -- ZERO physical reads on 310,803 probes -- for a near-identical fix count (CUBRID 1,105,561 = 0.9963x of PostgreSQL's 1,109,634). PostgreSQL's BAS_BULKREAD ring (heapam.c:397-410, chosen because lineitem's 1,125,128 blocks exceed NBuffers/4 = 262,144) confines the 8,790 MiB scan to a 256 kB ring per worker so the 2,483 MB orders relation stays fully resident in the same 8192 MB budget; CUBRID's scan pages go through pgbuf_unlatch_void_zone_bcb (page_buffer.c:6845, :6900-6934) into an LRU list with no per-scan strategy, and evict the join's inner side. Against IMP-008's 7.624 core-s (54.4% of the CPU excess) IMP-010 is worth about 1.66 core-s (11.8%), so it loses on magnitude but wins decisively on evidence quality and cost: it is the only Q06 candidate proved by a direct same-engine A/B with an arithmetically predicted control value (158,649 predicted vs 158,930 measured), and its fix is a two-field propagation rather than an executor specialization. Bands are disjoint by symbol from IMP-008 (kernel read path versus predicate/domain evaluation) so their effects add; they are NOT disjoint from IMP-007, which is why that relation is recorded as multiplicative.

IMP-005 - same subsystem boundary (pooled parallel-scan workers behaving differently from the serial path) and same fix locality (px_scan_task.cpp), but a statistics/observability defect rather than a buffer one; no effect overlap.

IMP-010.root_cause_title: A heap scan's newly read pages are inserted at the TOP of the session's private LRU list when the scan runs on the client transaction thread, but only into the MIDDLE of a round-robin SHARED LRU list when the same scan runs on pooled parallel-query workers, because a worker's thread entry is recycled with private_lru_index = -1 and the parallel-scan task never propagates its parent's LRU identity - so going parallel silently discards the buffer pool's scan-resistance and re-reads 2.88x the pages
IMP-010.upstream_precedent: No prior CBRD issue or PR that propagates the session's private LRU index into parallel-scan workers was identified in the pinned tree at 607f1ee9. The pattern of propagating per-session executor state into px workers IS established at px_scan_task.cpp:94 for m_px_orig_thread_entry, so this is an extension of an accepted pattern rather than a new one. On the PostgreSQL side the corresponding change is ancient and settled - BAS_BULKREAD ring buffers for large scans - which is why PostgreSQL's numbers here are DOP-independent; that is a precedent for the design, not for the CUBRID patch.
IMP-010.validation_criteria: (1) Q01-Q22 results byte-identical - mandatory for any buffer change even though placement cannot affect correctness. (2) Q06 CUBRID physical reads per statement fall from 458,209 to within 5% of the serial 158,930 at DOP 6, measured the same way (/proc/<cub_server>/io syscr delta / statement count) and cross-checked against the trace ioread counter. (3) The measured value stays within 5% of 158,930 at DOP 3 and DOP 12 as well, since DOP independence is the property being restored. (4) The rep_movs_alternative + filemap_* kernel band falls from 11.01% to under 5% of profiled self cost. (5) Q06 CUBRID median wall improves against 3.875 s under the same warm_establish + measure_block protocol with the WARM gate still CONVERGED, and the block-to-block spread does not exceed the 3.08% recorded here. (6) No regression in Q01/Q03/Q04 physical reads - those queries' IMP-002 evidence must be RE-MEASURED with this fix, because Q06 shows their 'pool cannot retain a marginally oversized working set' conclusion may in fact be this defect. (7) A high-DOP contention check: cub_server mutex/latch time on the private list must not rise above its current 3.50% buffer-manager band.

IMP-013.correctness_risk: Low. The LRU boost is a replacement-policy hint with no effect on visibility, latching, logging or recovery. No operator semantics change.

IMP-013.evidence_type: profile attribution (upper bound on the band). Not a direct A/B: no in-contract switch disables the LRU boost, and changing data_buffer_size would be a measurement-contract change requiring user approval.
IMP-013.explanation: CUBRID's LRU replacement policy needs list order, so it pays a mutex-protected unlink/relink plus zone rebalance on every unfix of a resident page; PostgreSQL's clock sweep needs no order, so it pays one atomic counter bump - which is why CUBRID's 6.6x smaller tuple-touch count only converts into a 16% CPU advantage instead of a wall win.
IMP-013.implementation_direction: Three options, cheapest first. (a) Extend the existing age-based suppression: pgbuf_lru_boost_bcb's own comment already documents 'if a page is quickly fixed several times, its age is really small ... we don't boost it', implemented in pgbuf_unlatch_bcb_upon_unfix; a random index-probe workload is the opposite case - a cold SINGLE touch of a zone-2/3 page - which that rule does not cover. Suppress the boost when the BCB's hit count since insertion is 1 and the fix was a read-only visibility fetch. (b) Batch the boost: record boost intent in the BCB and apply it under one mutex acquisition per N unfixes. (c) Replace the LRU lists with a clock sweep over the BCB array, removing the list and the per-list mutex entirely; freelist.c StrategyGetBuffer() is the reference shape.
measurement: F_cost = (CPU_C/W_C)/(CPU_P/W_P) = 1034.2 ns / 194.4 ns = 5.320850x, against F_work = W_C/W_P = 0.151371x, so F_cpu(native) = 0.805422x. CUBRID retires 0.7391x PostgreSQL's instructions (252.359 G vs 341.463 G) at 1.0909x the IPC (1.20 vs 1.10), and switches context 38.5x more often (2.734 K/s vs 71/s).

IMP-013.mechanism_cubrid: pgbuf_lru_boost_bcb() is called on unfix of any BCB that lives in LRU zone 2 or 3. It takes pthread_mutex_lock(&lru_list->mutex), calls pgbuf_remove_from_lru_list() to unlink the BCB from its current position, pgbuf_lru_add_bcb_to_top() to relink it at the head, and then pgbuf_lru_adjust_zone1() or pgbuf_lru_adjust_zones(), which walk the list to re-balance zone boundaries through pgbuf_bcb_change_zone(). On Q08's dominant path this runs once PER HEAP ROW: heap_get_visible_version() -> heap_clean_get_context -> pgbuf_unfix -> pgbuf_lru_boost_bcb, verified in the call graph at 5.38% of the parallel-query threads' cost. Q08 performs about 1.35 M fix/unfix pairs per statement (403,487 lineitem + 403,487 orders + 122,404 customer + 24,254 supplier heap lookups, each preceded by its index descent), so the list is reordered under a mutex about a million times per statement on pages that were already resident.
IMP-013.mechanism_postgresql: UnpinBuffer() / UnpinBufferNoOwner() decrement a PROCESS-LOCAL PrivateRefCountEntry->refcount and, only when it reaches zero, issue one pg_atomic_fetch_sub_u64(&buf->state, BUF_REFCOUNT_ONE). PinBuffer() bumps usagecount INSIDE the same compare-and-swap that takes the pin ('Default case: increase usagecount unless already max'). PostgreSQL's replacement algorithm is a clock sweep over the buffer array, so there is no ordered list to maintain, no per-list mutex to acquire and no zone rebalance to run. Searched src/storage/page_buffer.c for clock / sweep / usage_count / usagecount: CUBRID has no clock-sweep equivalent - the file implements private and shared LRU lists with zones 1/2/3.

q_evidence.Q11: Q11 REFUTES this candidate as a differentiator, and does so under the best possible conditions for it. In the saturated state BOTH engines take zero physical reads, so the buffer bands are pure hit-path cost with no miss confound: CUBRID 21.07% (pgbuf_fix_release 17.06, pgbuf_unfix 2.45, pgbuf_ordered_fix_release 0.71, pgbuf_ordered_unfix 0.47, pgbuf_set_dirty 0.38) plus 3.06% libpthread = 24.13%, against PostgreSQL 23.72% (hash_search_with_hash_value 12.73 - which the call graph resolves to BufTableLookup through StartReadBuffer -> PinBufferForBlock -> BufferAlloc, NOT to the HashAggregate - plus PinBuffer 4.41, LWLockAttemptLock 1.70, LockBufferInternal 0.76, UnpinBufferNoOwner 0.74, GetPrivateRefCountEntrySlow 0.70, LWLockRelease 0.68, StartReadBuffer 0.65, BufferLockUnlock 0.53, hash_bytes 0.47, ResourceOwnerForget 0.35). Shares are equal to 1.017x. Per page fix CUBRID spends 1339.0 ns of TOTAL QUERY CPU against PostgreSQL's 1475.2 ns, i.e. CUBRID is 1.1017x CHEAPER, and CUBRID's IPC is 1.65 against PostgreSQL's 1.39. Q11's CPU factor is therefore a fix-COUNT factor (F_work 1.496357x, owned by IMP-006) and not a per-fix cost factor. Q11 does not contradict Q08/Q09/Q10, where the unfix/boost path was measured on a different access pattern; it bounds the claim: on a single-threaded index-probe workload with no misses, CUBRID's buffer manager is not the more expensive one. IMP-013's priority should be re-derived from the queries where it IS separable, and Q11 added as a regression control.

alternative: IMP-010 - same subsystem, but the insertion-position defect for newly READ pages (private vs shared LRU chosen by thread identity). Fixing IMP-010 changes WHERE pages land; fixing IMP-013 changes WHETHER the list is touched at all on a hit.
containment: IMP-002 - that candidate is retention failure at a working set near the pool size and already lists pgbuf_lru_boost_bcb among the symbols in Q04's miss-path profile. IMP-013 is the HIT-path CPU cost of the same bookkeeping, a different quantity: IMP-002 costs physical reads, IMP-013 costs CPU on pages that were found.
IMP-007 - the synchronous single-page pread that serves the misses IMP-002 causes; IMP-013 is the cost of the hits.

IMP-013.risk: medium-high on performance regression: suppressing or batching boosts changes eviction order, so a workload whose hot set currently survives BECAUSE of aggressive boosting could start missing - and Q08 measures that a miss costs 0.4099 core-s per GiB of re-read. Option (a) is the only variant shippable without a full buffer-pool re-validation.
IMP-013.root_cause_title: Every page unfix on a HIT path performs mutex-protected LRU doubly-linked-list surgery plus zone rebalancing (pgbuf_lru_boost_bcb), so a plan that touches 6.6x fewer tuples than PostgreSQL's nets only a 16% total-CPU advantage: 27.41% of CUBRID's profile sits in pgbuf fix/unfix/LRU and 5.32% in libpthread, against PostgreSQL's 3.70% clock-sweep pin/unpin with no list and no mutex
IMP-013.upstream_precedent: No precedent in the pinned CUBRID history for removing or batching the LRU boost. The closest thing is the age-based suppression rule the same function's comment documents at page_buffer.c:10086-10098, which shows the cost was anticipated by the original author for a repeat-fix pattern - and is why option (a) is proposed first.
IMP-013.validation_criteria: pgbuf_lru_boost_bcb plus libpthread share on Q08 drops below 3% with pgbuf_fix_release unchanged; Q08 total_query_cpu drops by >= 0.3 core-s per statement; Q08 per-statement read-syscall count does NOT increase (the regression that matters - a worse eviction order shows up as more pool churn, which Q08 measures at 0.4099 core-s per GiB); Q01, Q03, Q04 and Q06 walls not regressed, since those are the sequential-scan queries whose retention IMP-002 already flags.

Step (2) risks divergence between the in-place comparison and the constructed-value comparison for collation-sensitive CHAR and for NULL handling, so it must be gated per type and validated by the full Q01-Q22 result set.

IMP-020.explanation: CUBRID spends 27.31 ns of total query CPU per attribute materialised against PostgreSQL's 5.45 ns -- 5.01x -- and then spends a further 1.5019 core-s tearing those values down, against PostgreSQL's 0.0800 core-s, because PostgreSQL never builds a value object in the first place. CUBRID loses this band while materialising THREE TIMES FEWER attributes than PostgreSQL.
IMP-020.implementation_direction: Two independent steps, cheapest first. (1) Hoist the per-row, per-attribute invariants out of heap_attrinfo_read_dbvalues(): a scan's attribute set, their domains and their disk sizes are fixed for the whole scan, so tp_domain_disk_size() and pr_type_from_id() should be resolved once into the HEAP_CACHE_ATTRINFO at scan open, and the DB_VALUE containers initialised once and REUSED, which removes db_value_domain_init()/pr_clear_value() from the per-row path entirely (band B). (2) Give the sarg path an attribute accessor that reads the value in place from the page image for the fixed-width types, so a predicate on a DATE or a CHAR(n) never needs a constructed DB_VALUE. Step (2) is the same direction as the accepted per-row-overhead reductions CBRD-26924 and CBRD-27041 already took for the scan path, extended from page/visibility handling to attribute handling.

IMP-020.root_cause_title: Per-row scan output is materialised into fully-typed DB_VALUEs: for every row the heap scan re-reads the MVCC/representation header, re-resolves each attribute's domain and disk size, calls a type-specific mr_data_readval_* to build a DB_VALUE, and afterwards tears each one down with pr_clear_value -- where PostgreSQL deforms the same tuple into a flat Datum/isnull array using cached attribute offsets, with no per-value type object, no per-value domain init and no per-value teardown at all
IMP-020.upstream_precedent: Yes, for the direction. a2f738e75 [CBRD-26924] 'Cut per-row overhead in non-fixed heap scan: COPY all-visible shortcut' (#7281) and b334446d6 [CBRD-27041] 'page-copy-then-peek scan' (#7441) are both accepted, and #7441 is IN the pinned build 607f1ee9 (SSOT section 3). Both reduce per-row scan overhead by hoisting work out of the row loop; this candidate applies the same principle to the attribute-materialisation step those two did not touch. No prior CBRD issue or PR was found that caches per-attribute domain or disk-size resolution across rows, or that reuses DB_VALUE containers across scan rows.
IMP-020.validation_criteria: (1) Q01-Q22 results byte-identical, in particular Q12's 2 rows MAIL 62071/93045 and SHIP 62426/93261 against sink/Q12-cubrid-headline-block1.out; (2) heap_attrinfo_read_dbvalues self-cost falls below 12% of the CUBRID profile on Q12 (from 21.64%) and the band-B symbols below 1.5% (from 6.31%), measured the same way with the same verified-PID perf attachment; (3) CUBRID instructions per lineitem row scanned fall from the measured 2,493 toward PostgreSQL's 1,398, recorded with perf stat over the same 60 s window; (4) Q12 CUBRID median wall improves against 4.039 s under the same warm_establish + measure_block protocol with the WARM gate still CONVERGED; (5) total_query_cpu does not increase.

IMP-021.correctness_risk: Medium. The change admits plans rather than forcing them, and qexec_groupby_index() is long-standing and already exercised by single-table queries, so no new execution path is introduced. The specific hazard is claiming an ordering across a join type that does not preserve it; validation criterion 5 pins that, and both engines already have the join-type guard written down.
cubrid_source: src/optimizer/query_planner.c:6014-6019 -- THE DEFECT. 'if (qo_is_iscan_from_groupby (plan) && !plan->plan_un.scan.index->head->groupby_skip) { qo_plan_release (plan); return 0; }'. At the moment this runs, the flag is still false for every plan that is not yet top-rooted, so the plan is released at birth.

src/optimizer/query_planner.c:6006-6012 -- THE ASYMMETRY, in the same function: the ORDER BY arm reads '!(plan->top_rooted ? plan->plan_un.scan.index->head->orderby_skip : qo_plan_is_orderby_skip_candidate (plan))', i.e. it has a pre-top-rooted candidate predicate. The GROUP BY arm has no such branch.

src/optimizer/query_planner.c:12559-12610 qo_plan_is_orderby_skip_candidate() -- the existing candidate predicate to mirror; it computes the sort list on the spot at :12603 via qo_plan_compute_iscan_sort_list().

src/optimizer/query_planner.c:1172-1175 -- the ONLY write of groupby_skip in the whole tree, inside qo_top_plan_new(), guarded by 'plan->plan_type == QO_PLANTYPE_SCAN'. A join plan can never satisfy it.
src/optimizer/query_planner.c:1192 -- the consequence: 'plan = qo_sort_new (plan, QO_UNORDERED, SORT_GROUPBY)', an unconditional sort.

src/optimizer/query_planner.c:9239-9246 -- where the QO_SCANMETHOD_INDEX_GROUPBY_SCAN plan is deliberately created for a node with no sargable terms once qo_validate_index_for_groupby() passes; :9283 qo_generate_seq_scan() then supplies the only surviving access path once the index plan is released.

src/optimizer/query_planner.c:12271-12291 -- qo_plan_compute_iscan_sort_list() ALREADY walks a join to its outer side ('case QO_PLANTYPE_JOIN: plan = plan->plan_un.join.outer;'), so the ability to read an order off a join is present and unused; :12310 then requires that leaf to be an interesting-order scan.

src/query/query_executor.c:16605-16609 -- the sort-free grouping routine qexec_groupby_index() is reachable only when xasl->spec_list->indexptr->groupby_skip is set, i.e. only when THIS xasl's own first access spec is the index scan carrying the flag; a join's xasl cannot satisfy that.
src/parser/xasl_generation.c:18399-18403 -- the '/* ---> skip GROUP BY */' plan annotation, gated on the same flag; its presence/absence is what the Q13 probes read.
IMP-021.difficulty_reason: A localized predicate addition whose exact analogue already exists three lines above it in the same function (the orderby_skip candidate branch at query_planner.c:6007-6008 with qo_plan_is_orderby_skip_candidate() at :12559-12610), and the ordering machinery it needs already walks joins (qo_plan_compute_iscan_sort_list() at :12279-12281). Not low, because it needs a correct join-type guard so an ordering is not claimed across a join type that does not preserve it.
IMP-021.effect_range: Direct same-engine A/B on CUBRID: 1.5617x (0.883 s -> 1.379 s, medians of 5) on an isolated 1,500,000-group aggregate where the ONLY change is adding one 1-row cross join, which cannot change the grouping work; the plan flips from 'iscan pk_customer_c_custkey (covers)' + '/* ---> skip GROUP BY */' to 'temp(group by)' + 'sort: 1 asc'. An explicit positive index hint cannot recover it (B' 1.371 s, plan text byte-identical to B), which is the runtime confirmation of the admission-time release. PostgreSQL's mirror A/B values the same optimization at 1.7268x (GroupAggregate 523.773 ms vs HashAggregate 904.450 ms over the same Index Only Scan), so the effect is not CUBRID-specific pessimism. On Q13 itself the addressable band is 16.4857% of traced CUBRID wall. NOT additive with IMP-015 or IMP-016.
IMP-021.evidence_event: inner GROUP BY node time and its temp materialisation. Q13 CUBRID trace: GROUPBY (time: 2202, hash: partial, sort: true, page: 20861, rows: 1500000) inside SELECT (time: 13187) inside a traced statement of 13,357 ms. Denominator: one Q13 statement. PostgreSQL's entire equivalent grouping apparatus (Partial GroupAggregate + Gather Merge + Finalize GroupAggregate) is 946.9 ms with no sort of the 15,337,604-row stream anywhere in the plan.
IMP-021.explanation: CUBRID tests a flag that cannot yet be true at the point of the test; PostgreSQL tests the ordering property itself.
IMP-021.implementation_direction: Mirror query_planner.c:6007-6008 in the GROUP BY arm: replace '!plan->plan_un.scan.index->head->groupby_skip' at :6015 with '!(plan->top_rooted ? plan->plan_un.scan.index->head->groupby_skip : qo_plan_is_groupby_skip_candidate (plan))', adding qo_plan_is_groupby_skip_candidate() as the exact analogue of qo_plan_is_orderby_skip_candidate() (:12559-12610) -- qo_plan_compute_iscan_sort_list() already accepts the group_by node it needs. Leave qo_top_plan_new() to set the flag on the surviving plan as it does today, so the executor and XASL paths are untouched. The change ADMITS a plan; the existing cost model still decides whether to use it.
measurement: Q13: R_wall 2.246313x (CUBRID 11.425999 s vs PostgreSQL 5.086557 s, medians of 3). Addressable band = inner GROUPBY 2,202 ms of 13,357 ms traced wall (16.4857%) + 20,861 temp pages (326 MiB). Direct A/B 1.5617x; hint-immune (B' 1.371 s). PostgreSQL mirror A/B 1.7268x. Capability probe q13-groupby-skip-probe.out shows '/* ---> skip GROUP BY */' present for a bare GROUP BY on customer/orders and absent as soon as the same GROUP BY sits above a join.

Real and well-localised, but roughly a third of what IMP-004 is worth on the same query (46.4-47.8% of Q13's CPU gap), so P1 rather than P0.
IMP-021.ranking_rationale: Ranked 4th of the five candidates carrying Q13 evidence. IMP-004 (46.4-47.8% of the 26.3964 core-s CPU gap), IMP-013 (12.1%) and IMP-020 (13.0%) all own larger measured bands of the CPU gap; IMP-021 owns 16.5% of CUBRID's traced WALL but only 5.12% of its CPU, because the grouping phase runs at fewer active units than the scan/join phase. Ranked above IMP-005, which is an instrumentation defect with no wall-clock value. It is nevertheless the only NEW root cause Q13 found, and the only one that is an optimizer plan-space defect rather than a per-row execution cost.

containment: Distinct from IMP-015: IMP-015 is about the sort-based group-by running single-threaded once it exists; IMP-021 is about the sort never being needed. Fixing IMP-021 removes the workload IMP-015 fails to parallelise, so the two are NOT additive on any query where both fire.

Distinct from IMP-016/IMP-017: those are about hash aggregation being abandoned or mis-parameterised. Q13's inner GROUPBY reports 'hash: partial', i.e. hash aggregation was NOT abandoned here; the cost is the materialisation the plan shape forces around it.
Distinct from IMP-011/IMP-014: those are about choosing the wrong JOIN. Q13's two engines choose the SAME join over the same FK index.

IMP-021.root_cause_title: A group-by-skip index scan plan is released at birth whenever the query contains a join, because qo_check_plan_on_info() tests index->head->groupby_skip -- a flag that is only ever written later, in qo_top_plan_new(), and only when the final top plan is itself a scan -- where the ORDER BY twin six lines above it tests a candidate predicate instead; so the sort-free streaming GROUP BY is unreachable behind any join and an unconditional SORT_GROUPBY is inserted
IMP-021.upstream_precedent: Yes, in this very source tree: CBRD-26906, cited in the comment at query_planner.c:9257-9260 ('an interesting-order (group-by / order-by skip) index scan also means the hinted index is usable, so a positive index hint that only provides ordering (no key-range) still suppresses the sequential scan below'). That change taught the planner that an index whose only contribution is ordering is a real alternative on the HINT path; IMP-021 extends the same reasoning to the ADMISSION path. CBRD-24044 is referenced in the adjacent comment at :9274-9275 as the earlier state of the same code.
validation_criteria: Q13's CUBRID estimated plan shows an ordered customer access with '/* ---> skip GROUP BY */' and no 'sort: 1 asc' above the join, and the trace's 20,861 temp pages go to 0.
Result equivalence re-proved by the SSOT section 11 gate: 46 rows, exact ordered match, and the ten ground-truth cardinalities G0-G8 unchanged.
The section 8-c A/B collapses toward 1.0x: 'select c_custkey, count(*) from customer, region where r_regionkey = 0 group by c_custkey' approaches the 0.883 s of the join-free form.
No plan regression on Q01-Q12, re-checked with the estimated-plan harness; the change only admits an alternative.

Left-outer-join null-extension semantics preserved: the ordering is taken from the OUTER (preserved) side only. query_planner.c:12621-12628 already documents the RIGHT-outer restriction the new predicate must respect, exactly as PostgreSQL's build_join_pathkeys() does at pathkeys.c:1303-1306.
