source_contrast:
Four rows, concrete file:line both sides, absence claims searched not assumed.

(1) Parallelism of a sort-based GROUP BY. CUBRID: src/storage/external_sort.c sort_check_parallelism(), SORT_GROUP_BY/SORT_ANALYTIC branch returns 1 whenever px->hash_eligible is set; hash_eligible originates from src/parser/xasl_generation.c:16556-16568 at XASL-generation time from query SHAPE only, never re-evaluated after the executor degrades to sorting at runtime (hash:partial in q18-trace-cubrid.out). Consequence: the 29,563ms group-by runs at 1 unit. PostgreSQL: src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c implements partial/final aggregation as ordinary parallel-aware plan nodes; the planner emits Partial GroupAggregate -> Gather Merge -> Finalize GroupAggregate, so aggregation parallelism is a PLAN property independent of whether hashing was chosen -- the noidx anchor runs Partial HashAggregate at loops=6 and finalises through Gather Merge. Difference: CUBRID's sort-based aggregation has no parallel path reachable for a hash-eligible query, independent of what the executor actually did at runtime; class structural absence.

(2) Deduplication of an IN(subquery) result. CUBRID: src/parser/type_checking.c:5037 unconditionally sets arg2->info.query.all_distinct = PT_DISTINCT for any range expression whose arg2 is a query ('duplicates are not relevant'), no check for an already-distinct subquery; QFILE_FLAG_DISTINCT builds a real extra sort pass (src/query/list_file.c:1284-1300), visible as temp(distinct) above temp(group by), costed 1,308,583 vs 1,070,742. PostgreSQL: src/backend/optimizer/plan/planmain.c:237 calls reduce_unique_semijoins() -> analyzejoins.c:1042 rel_supports_distinctness() -> :1118 innerrel_is_unique() -> :1524 rel_is_distinct_for() -> :1178 query_is_distinct_for() -> :1328, whose :1372-1389 proves distinctness because the subquery has a GROUP BY covering the join columns, then deletes the semijoin's SpecialJoinInfo so SEMI becomes a plain inner join (Inner Unique:true). Difference: CUBRID has no already-distinct proof and cannot drop the DISTINCT it added -- measured Q18 effect +0.188%, inside the 1.6% error band, NOT an effect on this query (the DISTINCT runs after HAVING on 624 rows). Class structural absence.

(3) Evaluation count of an uncorrelated IN subquery. CUBRID: src/optimizer/rewriter/query_rewrite_subquery.c:165 -> mq_make_derived_spec() (src/parser/view_transform.c:10918) materialises the subquery as one derived spec av1861, evaluated ONCE and joined by key. PostgreSQL: src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c:1341 convert_ANY_sublink_to_join() pulls the sublink up as a JOIN_SEMI sub-select RTE; when the resulting path lands on the INNER side of a Merge Join inside a parallel region it is re-executed per unit (rows=59985038.00 loops=6) because inner join inputs are not partitioned. Difference: CUBRID does 59,986,052 subquery row-fetches, PostgreSQL does 359,910,228 for identical logical work -- this IS the whole of F_plan 0.734231x. Class: same stage, lower measured cost (CUBRID better).

(4) Aggregation memory budget. CUBRID: max_agg_hash_size=2.0M and sort_buffer_size=2.0M (server defaults) while the campaign grants data_buffer_size=8192M; the subquery must form 15,000,000 groups, a 2MB hash table holds a negligible fraction, executor degrades to sorting and spills 422,017 temp pages / 459,086 ioreads; max_agg_hash_size is not session-settable (ERROR: Cannot change system parameter). PostgreSQL: sizes hash aggregation from work_mem and, when it does not fit, PLANS Partial HashAggregate with Planned Partitions:16 -- a spill strategy chosen and costed by the planner, not a runtime collapse into a global sort. Difference: the 8GB buffer budget is unreachable by the operator that dominates Q18; raising only the session-settable half (sort_buffer_size 2M->256M) cuts spill pages 65.5% and the traced statement 6.93%. Class: same stage, lower measured cost.

Absence-search record: searched src/optimizer/, src/parser/, src/query/ for an already-distinct proof; patterns query_is_distinct (0), is_distinct_for (0), redundant.*distinct (0), remove.*distinct (0), distinct.*redundant (0), distinct_elim (0), already.*distinct (0), eliminate.*distinct (2 hits, both executor on-the-fly dedup comments, not a planner proof), unique_for (7 hits, all FK/index grammar and execute_schema.c error paths). Only site resetting all_distinct=PT_ALL is type_checking.c:7056 inside pt_to_false_subquery() (folding a provably-empty subquery), unrelated.
causal_decomposition_narrative:
Where Q18's time actually goes -- subquery input scan: CUBRID 11,829ms/6 units/partitioned; PostgreSQL native 35,432ms/6 units/REPLICATED 6x; PostgreSQL-noidx 653ms/unit/6 units/partitioned. Subquery aggregation: CUBRID 29,563ms/1 unit/422,017 spill pages; PostgreSQL native folded into the index scan (streaming, no sort); PostgreSQL-noidx 9,962ms/unit partial+finalise. Outer join+final agg: CUBRID 30ms; PostgreSQL native ~1,200ms; PostgreSQL-noidx ~13,000ms (extra full lineitem seq scan). Traced statement totals: CUBRID 41,430ms, PostgreSQL native 48,473ms, PostgreSQL-noidx 33,136ms.

Explanations considered and rejected, with the rejecting number:
- 'CUBRID wins because its optimizer is better here' -- rejected as a general claim, accepted only as F_plan. On the controlled pair CUBRID is 1.140993x worse on CPU and 1.069863x worse on units; its win is 0.734231x of plan shape on PostgreSQL's own side of the comparison.
- 'CUBRID's redundant DISTINCT is a real cost' -- rejected by direct same-engine A/B: 34.570999s with it vs 34.505999s without, +0.188%, roughly one within-block sd (0.075s), well inside the 1.6% error band. The optimizer estimates it at +22% of subquery cost (1,308,583 vs 1,070,742) only because it also mis-estimates the subquery at 59,986,052 rows; DISTINCT actually runs after HAVING, on 624 rows.
- 'CUBRID's 14.9M-row estimate for av1861 costs it something' -- rejected: wrong by ~24,000x (14,929,885 vs 624) yet selects the same join order/access paths a correct estimate would select; outer pipeline costs 30ms of 41,430ms.
- 'PostgreSQL is slower because of physical I/O' -- rejected: read_bytes delta is 0 on every PostgreSQL block; the 5,689,168 heap_blks_read are shared-buffer misses served by the OS page cache, and 48.67% of PostgreSQL's cycles are buffer lock/unlock, not I/O wait.
- 'Clearing hash_eligible will unblock the serial group-by' -- rejected by direct A/B, the most instructive negative result: the only user-reachable lever, /*+ NO_HASH_AGGREGATE */, made CUBRID SLOWER (40.173998s vs 37.452998s, +7.3%), TWU FALLING 2.7041->1.8912, serial tail RISING 12.548s->30.578s. Trace shows why: GROUPBY time:43073 hash:false sort:true page:139848 against native time:29563 hash:partial page:422017 -- the hint removes the partial hash pre-aggregation that reduces 59,986,052 rows toward 15,000,000 groups, and the sort did not become parallel anyway. The hint changes two things at once, so it cannot isolate sort_check_parallelism(); it refutes the naive fix rather than measuring the real one.

Bound on the serial-group-by opportunity (upper bound, not a measurement, because no switch isolates it): CUBRID's block spends 89.10s of 140.50s at ~1 unit (22.28s/statement) and 44.11s at ~6 units. If the serial phase were perfectly parallelised to 6 units (ignoring merge/gather overhead), the statement would fall from 37.45s to roughly 37.45 - 22.28 + 22.28/6 ~= 18.9s, i.e. at most ~1.98x. Against PostgreSQL's best plan (30.681412s) that would move CUBRID from 1.22x behind to ~1.62x ahead.

improvement_relations.relation: added - existing root cause, Q relation and evidence added, campaign-strongest evidence
improvement_relations.note: sort_check_parallelism() unconditionally refuses parallelism for a SORT_GROUP_BY whenever the query was marked hash-aggregate-eligible, even after the executor abandons hash aggregation at runtime. Q18 mechanism: xasl_generation.c:16556-16568 sets g_hash_eligible=true for Q18's subquery purely because sum() is hash-aggregatable; at runtime the 2MB max_agg_hash_size cannot hold the 15,000,000 groups the ground truth confirms, so the executor degrades to a sort (hash:partial, 422,017 spill pages); external_sort.c sort_check_parallelism()'s SORT_GROUP_BY branch then returns 1 because px->hash_eligible is still set, so the fallback sort runs single-threaded. PostgreSQL contrast: aggregation parallelism is a plan property (nodeAgg.c partial/final nodes under Gather Merge), independent of hashing -- Partial HashAggregate loops=6 in the noidx plan. Quantified effect: 89.10s of the 140.50s CUBRID block at ~1 active unit (63.4%, time-weighted from 1,253 real intervals); trace attributes 29,563ms of the 41,430ms statement to that GROUPBY; profile attributes it to the transaction comm (18.36 of 77.55 resolved points, led by qfile_compare_partial_sort_record 3.27%, sort_run_merge 0.80%). Upper bound on the fix: ~1.98x. Evidence type: profile attribution + upper bound, NOT direct A/B (the only available switch, NO_HASH_AGGREGATE, changes two things at once and made CUBRID 7.3% SLOWER -- a measured rejection of that naive alternative, TWU falling 2.7041->1.8912). Implementation direction: re-evaluate the parallel decision on the actual runtime state instead of the XASL-time flag -- consult the executor's hash-aggregate outcome (hash:partial / HS_REJECT_ALL) at the point sort_listfile is entered, rather than the planner's g_hash_eligible. Risk: medium -- parallel sort-group-by already exists for non-hash-eligible queries, so risk is scheduling/worker-pool pressure, not correctness; a query whose hash aggregation succeeds must keep its current path. Validation: on Q18, TWU rises above ~4 with unchanged results and unchanged spill page count; q18-groundtruth values byte-identical; no regression where hash aggregation completes in memory. Ranked #1 for Q18: governs 63.4% of the block wall, versus IMP-016/017's spill-size effect (6.93% measured) and the redundant DISTINCT's 0.188% (inside the error band).

causal_decomposition_narrative: The 6.2373x plan factor is the whole of Q20's cross-engine result and it is PostgreSQL's. It decomposes in three measured steps: PostgreSQL drives from supplier rather than part, so the ps_availqty > (SubPlan) filter is applied to ~250,943 rather than 86,204 partsupp rows and the correlated aggregate runs 247,287 times instead of 86,204 (2.8686x); those extra probes scatter over an 11 GB index and push the working set past shared_buffers, giving 589,094 physical page reads per statement instead of 0; and those reads cost 34.27% of the profile, 2.3748 core-s per statement, collapsing IPC from 1.24 to 0.92. Together CPU_P/CPU_Pc = 6.1372x against a wall ratio of 6.2373x. REJECTED BY MEASUREMENT: (a) 'CUBRID wins because it parallelises' -- 90.3% of its statement is serial, F_units is worth only 1.2026x and the matched PostgreSQL plan is equally serial; (b) 'CUBRID wins because it does less I/O' -- at matched plan BOTH sides take zero physical reads, so the I/O difference is a consequence of the plan choice already counted inside F_plan and counting it again would double-count; (c) 'CUBRID's optimizer made a better decision' -- CUBRID makes no decision, query_rewrite_subquery.c:165 appends a derived spec unconditionally and a derived spec cannot be reordered, so the good plan is the ONLY plan CUBRID can build; (d) 'the low-residency 3.16 s level is CUBRID's true WARM level' -- rejected by a cold-pool A/B in which the identical statement reaches full residency within ONE statement from an empty pool; (e) 'the residency hysteresis is IMP-018's private-LRU cap' -- rejected by the same A/B, in which a single cold session accumulates 7.5 GB in one statement and a foreign session's touch changes nothing; (f) 'PostgreSQL's period-2 alternation is host noise' -- rejected by lag-1 autocorrelation -0.9092, disjoint phases, and an exact one-to-one tie to a 59,357-page read difference.

Q20's headline is a 3.4326x CUBRID WIN (1.992000 s against 6.837673 s), but the report's central claim is that the win is entirely a PostgreSQL PLAN-CHOICE defect and not a CUBRID execution advantage: measured against PostgreSQL's own better plan -- a MATERIALIZED CTE expressing the shape CUBRID's rewriter forces, byte-identical result, 1.096253 s -- CUBRID is 1.8171x SLOWER, using 2.1853x the CPU on exactly 86,204 correlated-subquery executions per side (F_work = 1.000000 measured, not assumed). plan_comparison_summary: CUBRID: qo_rewrite_subqueries() converts each uncorrelated IN into a DERIVED SPEC appended to FROM, recursively, so the query becomes a bottom-up pipeline of three nested av1861 specs -- sscan part (5 parallel workers) -> temp(distinct) 21,551 -> idx-join into partsupp via fk_partsupp_part with the correlated aggregate as a sarg (subqs: 0) -> temp(distinct) 44,482 -> idx-join supplier/nation -> temp(order by). A derived spec is materialised bottom-up and is NOT a relation the join-order search may reorder. PostgreSQL native: convert_ANY_sublink_to_join() pulls each sublink up as JOIN_SEMI, leaving the order to the cost model, which drives from supplier -- Nested Loop Semi Join over a Gather Merge of 4,054 Canadian suppliers, Index Scan idx_fk_partsupp_supplier (loops=4054) carrying the ps_availqty > (SubPlan) filter, then part_pkey (loops=168,171). PostgreSQL controlled: Seq Scan part (21,551 of 2,000,000) -> Index Scan idx_fk_partsupp_part (loops=21,551) -> SubPlan loops=86,204 -> Unique 44,482 -> Hash Join to supplier x nation. The controlled plan matches CUBRID's shape node for node.

source_contrast: 1) What an uncorrelated IN becomes. CUBRID src/optimizer/rewriter/query_rewrite.c:292 -> query_rewrite_subquery.c:40 (CNF walk), :73-75 (admits PT_IS_IN), :123 (requires correlation_level == 0), :165 mq_make_derived_spec() (src/parser/view_transform.c:10918), :219 recursion into the new spec. PostgreSQL src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c:1341 convert_ANY_sublink_to_join() with :1450 jointype = JOIN_SEMI. CUBRID FIXES the order at rewrite time; PostgreSQL DEFERS it to the cost model. Class: structural absence of the choice itself. 2) Why PostgreSQL's cost model prefers the worse order. src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c:636 tuples_fetched = clamp_row_est(indexSelectivity * baserel->tuples) and :800 cpu_run_cost += cpu_per_tuple * tuples_fetched charge the SubPlan correctly on every index-matched tuple -- the defect is the input: n_distinct(partsupp.ps_partkey) = 444,930 against a true 2,000,000 (correlation 0.9999991) while ps_suppkey is accurate to 0.29%. PostgreSQL therefore believes each part-driven probe fetches 17.98 rows instead of 4, costing 152.5 per loop (planned 159.48) instead of ~40.9, and ranks 3,288,816 against 2,812,921 the wrong way. Class: same stage, lower measured cost (CUBRID better). 3) Per-page buffer handling. CUBRID src/storage/page_buffer.c pgbuf_fix_release + pgbuf_lru_boost_bcb (mutex + doubly-linked-list surgery + zone rebalancing on unfix), 0.5944 core-s for 1,300,830 fetches, against PostgreSQL BufTableLookup -> hash_search_with_hash_value + PinBuffer (hash probe + atomic refcount, no list, no mutex), 0.3643 core-s for 1,033,307 fetches -- 1.30x more CPU per page fetch. 4) Row materialisation. CUBRID src/storage/heap_file.c:10464 heap_attrinfo_read_dbvalues and friends build fully-typed DB_VALUEs per row, 0.4720 core-s, against PostgreSQL src/backend/executor/execTuples.c tts_buffer_heap_getsomeattrs deforming into a flat Datum/isnull array, 0.3474 core-s -- 1.36x. 5) Predicate evaluation. CUBRID src/query/query_evaluator.c:1666 eval_pred() and :152 eval_value_rel_cmp() re-walk and re-dispatch a generic PRED_EXPR per row, 0.2838 core-s, against PostgreSQL execExprInterp.c ExecInterpExpr on quals compiled once into type-specialised ExprEvalSteps, 0.1142 core-s -- 2.49x. 6) Parallelising the dominant operator. CUBRID src/query/parallel/px_parallel.cpp:85-109 case parallel_type::SUBQUERY, :89-92 auto_degree = 1. PostgreSQL does not parallelise a MATERIALIZED CTE either. Class: common to both engines.
